name: LINC — Language Instruction for Newcomers to Canada
description: LINC is a free language training program funded by the Government of Canada for eligible adult newcomers. It provides English and French language classes at all levels — beginner, intermediate, and advanced — at no cost to permanent residents and protected persons. Classes are offered at over 400 locations across Canada, including community colleges, school boards, and immigrant-serving organizations. LINC also provides free childcare for children aged 12 months to 11 years while parents attend class. The program covers Canadian Language Benchmarks (CLB) levels 1 through 7, helping newcomers develop the language skills needed for daily life, employment, and community integration.
eligibility: Permanent residents and protected persons (convention refugees) aged 17 or older; must complete a language assessment through an IRCC-designated assessment centre; economic class immigrants eligible for 6 years after becoming permanent residents (as of April 2026); Canadian citizens and temporary residents are not eligible
amount: Free (fully government-funded — no tuition or fees)
applicationProcess: Contact a local IRCC-designated language assessment centre to take a free language assessment. Based on results, you will be placed at an appropriate CLB level and referred to a nearby LINC provider. Register directly with the provider. Classes are available full-time, part-time, and online. No application deadline — enrollment is continuous throughout the year.
geographicScope: Canada — all provinces and territories, 400+ locations nationwide
documentsRequired: Proof of permanent residency or protected person status (PR card, confirmation of permanent residence, or refugee claim document), government-issued photo ID, language assessment results from an IRCC-designated centre

name: France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship Program
organization: French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs
description: The France Excellence Eiffel Scholarship Program enables top international students to pursue master's and PhD programs at French higher education institutions. Developed by the French Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs, the program provides a monthly stipend of approximately 1,181 euros for master's students and 1,700 euros for PhD candidates, along with international round-trip airfare, health insurance coverage, housing assistance, and cultural activities. The scholarship covers 12 to 36 months of study depending on the program level. Eiffel scholars join a prestigious network and gain access to French academic excellence across fields including law, economics, management, political science, engineering, and the sciences.
eligibility: Non-French nationals from any country; master's applicants must be 29 or younger; PhD applicants must be 35 or younger; applicants must not have previously received an Eiffel scholarship; applicants cannot apply directly — must be nominated by a French higher education institution; priority given to students from developing countries and emerging economies
amount: €1,181/month (master's) or €1,700/month (PhD) plus international airfare, health insurance, housing search assistance, and cultural activities
applicationProcess: Students cannot apply directly. First, contact the French institution where you wish to study and confirm they will nominate you. The institution submits the application through the Campus France online portal during the annual call (typically October to January). Results are announced in late March. Candidates must demonstrate academic excellence and a clear study project aligned with France's international priorities.
geographicScope: France — all participating French higher education institutions
documentsRequired: Valid passport, academic transcripts and degree certificates, CV, study project / research proposal, two academic reference letters, proof of language proficiency (French or English depending on program), motivation letter submitted by the nominating institution

name: VLIR-UOS Training and Masters Scholarships (Belgium)
organization: Flemish Interuniversity Council — University Development Cooperation (VLIR-UOS)
description: VLIR-UOS provides full scholarships for students and professionals from developing countries to attend short training programs (1 to 4 months) and English-taught master's programs (1 to 2 years) at Flemish universities and university colleges in Belgium. The scholarships cover tuition fees, a monthly living allowance, international airfare, accommodation, and health insurance. Training programs focus on development-relevant subjects such as public health, agriculture, water management, education, and governance. VLIR-UOS aims to strengthen the capacity of institutions and individuals in the Global South through academic cooperation and knowledge exchange.
eligibility: Nationals of VLIR-UOS partner countries (54 countries in Africa, Asia, and Latin America); for training: professionals with relevant work experience; for master's: bachelor's degree holders with at least 2 years of professional experience; maximum age 35 for master's programs and 45 for training; must return to home country after completion
amount: Full scholarship — tuition, €1,100/month living allowance, international airfare, accommodation, and health insurance
applicationProcess: Browse available programs on the VLIR-UOS scholarship portal. Submit an online application through the specific program's page, typically between October and February for the following academic year. Applications require academic transcripts, a motivation letter, CV, and employer endorsement. Shortlisted candidates may be interviewed. Selection is competitive and based on academic merit, professional relevance, and development impact potential.
geographicScope: Belgium — Flemish universities and university colleges (KU Leuven, Ghent University, VUB, University of Antwerp, Hasselt University, and associated colleges)
documentsRequired: Bachelor's degree certificate and transcripts, CV, motivation letter, proof of professional experience (minimum 2 years for master's), employer endorsement letter, valid passport, English proficiency certificate (IELTS or TOEFL), medical certificate

name: Alberta Settlement, Integration and Language Projects Grants
organization: Government of Alberta — Ministry of Immigration and Multiculturalism
description: The Alberta government funds settlement, integration, and language projects that help newcomers integrate into Alberta communities and the Canadian labour market. Grants are awarded under two streams: Building Community Capacity (helping communities attract, welcome, and retain newcomers) and Supporting Labour Market Attachment (funding training projects that provide skill development with a language component). These projects include workplace language training, bridging programs that combine language instruction with professional skills development, mentorship programs, and community-based settlement support. Funded organizations include school boards, post-secondary institutions, immigrant-serving agencies, and community nonprofits across Alberta.
eligibility: Newcomers to Alberta including permanent residents, refugees, and temporary foreign workers; projects serve immigrants who need language support combined with job skills training or community integration; applicant organizations must be Alberta-based nonprofits, school boards, or post-secondary institutions
amount: Varies by project — typical grants range from $50,000 to $502,500 per year
applicationProcess: Eligible organizations submit proposals through the Alberta government's grant portal during open funding rounds. Applications must describe the target newcomer population, proposed activities, expected outcomes, and budget. Funded projects typically run for one to three years. Individual newcomers access services through funded organizations — there is no individual application process; contact a local immigrant-serving agency to access funded programs.
geographicScope: Alberta, Canada — communities across the province
documentsRequired: For organizations: project proposal, budget, letters of support, organizational capacity documentation. For individual newcomers accessing services: proof of immigration status (PR card, work permit, or refugee document), Alberta residency

name: Italian Government Scholarships for Foreign Students
organization: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
description: The Italian Government offers scholarships to foreign citizens and Italian citizens living abroad to pursue higher education and advanced vocational training courses in Italy. Scholarships are awarded for master's degree programs, advanced vocational training, courses in Italian language and culture, and research projects at accredited Italian institutions. The scholarship provides a monthly stipend, tuition fee waiver at public universities, and health insurance coverage. Italy is a major destination for students seeking education in art, design, architecture, engineering, medicine, and the humanities. The program supports academic mobility and cultural exchange, with particular attention to students from developing countries.
eligibility: Foreign citizens and Italian citizens residing abroad; must hold a bachelor's degree or equivalent for master's programs; must meet Italian language requirements (B2 level for Italian-taught programs) or English proficiency for English-taught programs; age limit varies by program but generally under 35 for master's and research scholarships
amount: €900/month stipend plus tuition waiver at public universities and health insurance
applicationProcess: Apply through the Italian Ministry's Study in Italy portal during the annual call (typically opens in spring for the following academic year). Submit an online application with academic documents, language certificates, and a study plan. Applications are reviewed by the Italian diplomatic mission in the applicant's country of residence. Shortlisted candidates receive a scholarship award letter needed for the student visa application.
geographicScope: Italy — all accredited public universities and recognized vocational training institutions
documentsRequired: Valid passport, bachelor's degree certificate and academic transcripts (with certified translation), Italian or English language certificate (CILS/CELI B2 or IELTS/TOEFL), study plan or research proposal, CV, passport-size photograph, Declaration of Value from the Italian embassy in the applicant's country

name: Washington State FAP Employment & Training Program for Refugees
organization: Washington State Department of Social and Health Services (DSHS)
description: The Washington State Food Assistance Program Employment & Training (FAP E&T) program provides employment readiness opportunities for immigrants and refugees receiving state food assistance. The program funds organizations that deliver job skills training, career counseling, resume preparation, interview skills workshops, English language instruction for the workplace, professional certification support, and job placement services. FAP E&T specifically targets immigrants and refugees who are ineligible for federal SNAP benefits but receive Washington State Food Assistance Program benefits, helping them overcome barriers to employment through culturally and linguistically appropriate services. The program supports participants in obtaining living-wage employment and achieving economic self-sufficiency.
eligibility: Immigrants and refugees in Washington State receiving Food Assistance Program (FAP) benefits; includes legal permanent residents in their first 5 years, refugees, asylees, and other qualified immigrants; must be at least 18 years old and authorized to work in the United States
amount: Free services (program funded by Washington State; no cost to participants)
applicationProcess: Contact a local DSHS Community Services Office or an immigrant-serving organization funded by the FAP E&T program. A case worker will assess eligibility based on FAP benefit status and create an individualized employment plan. Services are available on a rolling basis. Organizations interested in providing FAP E&T services can apply through the DSHS Office of Refugee and Immigrant Assistance during open funding periods.
geographicScope: Washington State, United States — King County, Pierce County, Spokane County, and other areas with significant immigrant populations
documentsRequired: Proof of FAP benefit enrollment, government-issued ID, work authorization documentation, Social Security number or application receipt
